{:db/id 17592186133828 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186133643 :question/id #uuid "25d6bb34-eeb6-5bb7-8b66-0e6424244eeb" :question/math-academy-id "e-6285" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle\int\limits_C\mathbf F\cdot \textrm d \mathbf r

$$
\int\limits_C\mathbf F\cdot \textrm d \mathbf r  = \int_a^b\mathbf F(\mathbf r (t))\cdot \mathbf r'(t)\,\textrm d t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x = 1 + 2t, \qquad y = 1 - t .
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) & =y\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(x+y)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\  & =(1-t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+((1+2t)+(1-t))\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\  & =(1-t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(t+2)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t)\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)\mathbf{j} \\  & =2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t))\cdot {\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t) & =((1-t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(t+2)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j})\cdot (2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}) \\  & =(1-t)\cdot 2+(t+2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =2-2t-t-2 \\  & =-3t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r})\cdot \text{d}\mathbf{r} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{r}(t))\cdot {\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t)\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-3t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathrm{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}-0 \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}

where $\mathbf F(x,y)=x\,\mathbf i+(y-1)\,\mathbf j$ and $C$ is the path $\mathbf r(t)=t\sin t\,\mathbf i+t\cos t\,\mathbf j$ for $0\le t\le\pi$." :question/worked-solution "Use the parametrized line-integral formula:

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}

&=t\sin^2t+t^2\sin t\cos t\\
&\quad +t\cos^2t-t^2\sin t\cos t\\
&\quad -\cos t+t\sin t\\
&=t-\cos t+t\sin t.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}(-t\cos t)=-\cos t+t\sin t.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r

&=\frac{\pi^2}{2}-\pi(-1)-0\\

$$
{\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r
$$ given that $F(x,y)=(2 y - 1)\,i+(2 x - y + 1)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(- 2 t - 2)\,i+(- t - 1)\,j$ for $t\in[0,1].$

*Hint:* Use

$$
\int_C F\cdot\mathrm d r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt
$$." :question/worked-solution "We will use the formula

$$

$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- 2 t - 2,\quad y=- t - 1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t)) \\ \begin{aligned} &=(2 y - 1)\,i+(2 x - y + 1)\,j \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\left(2 \left(- t - 1\right) - 1\right)\,i \\ &{} +\left(2 \left(- 2 t - 2\right) - \left(- t - 1\right) + 1\right)\,j\end{aligned} \\ &=(- 2 t - 3)\,i+(- 3 t - 2)\,j\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t - 2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- t - 1)\,j \\  & =(-2)\,i+(-1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left({(- 2 t - 3)\,i+(- 3 t - 2)\,j}\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left({(-2)\,i+(-1)\,j}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(- 2 t - 3)\cdot(-2)+(- 3 t - 2) \\ &{} \cdot(-1)\end{aligned} \\ &=\left({4 t + 6}\right)+\left({3 t + 2}\right) \\ &=7 t + 8\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:
